title: First-class Alias Creation Delivery
summary: give New Alias its own validated mutation contract so ordinary creation no longer depends on bulk alias import
content_html:
First-class Alias Creation Delivery

Complete Result

New Alias creates exactly one canonical alias through a first-class server mutation and no longer calls the bulk tag-alias import route.

The user-visible workflow remains the same: enter an alias key and description, select canonical targets, create, then reload canonical aliases and record activity evidence.

Why This Comes Before Removal

The current browser create path sends a one-alias payload to the import endpoint in add mode. Bulk alias import cannot be removed safely until ordinary creation has its own contract.

In Scope

  • Add a focused alias-create planner and server request/response contract through the Studio tag mutation boundary.
  • Enforce slug-safe alias identity, duplicate rejection, description normalization, canonical target existence, and one target per group.
  • Add one alias without rewriting unrelated alias records.
  • Use the existing allowlisted atomic write and activity owners, with a distinct create action rather than import-shaped evidence.
  • Switch the New Alias browser workflow to the create operation.
  • Preserve the supported manual JSON patch fallback when the local write service is unavailable.
  • Cover service, route, browser payload, runtime configuration, and activity behavior with focused tests.

Not In Scope

  • Removing bulk alias or registry import UI and endpoints; that belongs to the final removal delivery.
  • Changing alias edit, delete, promotion, tag demotion, or assignments.
  • Adding new alias semantics or changing existing canonical alias records.
  • Changing the offline assignment-session workflow.

Likely Authority

  • studio/services/tags/tag_source_model.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_alias_mutations.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_write_transactions.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/aliases.py
  • studio/app/server/studio/studio_tags_api.py
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-aliases-service.js
  • studio/app/frontend/js/tag-aliases.js
  • Studio runtime service and activity configuration
  • focused alias planner, route, workflow, and smoke tests

These are inspection starting points, not a requirement to change every file.

Completion And Evidence

  • A valid request adds exactly one normalized alias and leaves all existing aliases unchanged.
  • Invalid key, duplicate key, missing target, unknown target, duplicate target, and repeated target-group requests fail before any write.
  • New Alias no longer requests the alias-import endpoint in direct-write mode.
  • Successful creation reloads canonical aliases and records one create-alias activity action.
  • Manual patch mode still produces one valid alias fragment without implying that it was written.
  • Focused planner/API tests, route/module integration checks, and a manual New Alias interaction pass support only these claims.
  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-aliases.json is unchanged by delivery implementation and verification.

Durable Destination

Transfer the shipped create workflow and extension boundary to Tag Aliases.
